external_entities.name: duty engineer
external_entities.description: An engineer who uses the dispatch console.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.
external_entities.notes: The text describes duty engineers as users of the platform; how they authenticate is not recorded.

external_entities.name: scheduling partner
external_entities.description: Another company that publishes tomorrow's planned work.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company, publishes tomorrow's planned work.
external_entities.notes: The partner's authentication arrangements are not recorded.

processes.name: dispatch console
processes.description: A single-page JavaScript app opened by duty engineers and used to call the dispatch API and receive live job status.
processes.source_excerpt: The console is a single-page JavaScript app and our corporate web host serves it.
processes.notes: Nobody wrote down how an engineer signs in to it. The console and API are served from different origins; CORS configuration is not recorded.

processes.name: dispatch API
processes.description: An API running in the production control plane that the console and importer use to access dispatch data.
processes.source_excerpt: The dispatch API runs in the production control plane.
processes.notes: The control plane is not reachable from the internet. The API's authentication mechanism is not otherwise described.

processes.name: schedule importer
processes.description: A process that pulls the scheduling partner's SOAP feed, parses XML documents, archives them, and posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API.
processes.source_excerpt: Our schedule importer runs on the corporate network.
processes.notes: The importer presents an API token that was issued when it was built and has not been rotated.

data_stores.name: dispatch database
data_stores.description: A database containing job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order.
data_stores.source_excerpt: That database holds the job orders, the crew names and the crew mobile numbers.
data_stores.notes: Every job order carries the token or session that created it, and nothing about the person behind that token. Protection at rest is not recorded.

data_stores.name: schedule archive
data_stores.description: A folder on the corporate file store where downloaded scheduling documents are written.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive, a folder on the corporate file store.
data_stores.notes: The text names the archive as a folder on the corporate file store but does not place it in a network zone. Protection at rest is not recorded.

data_flows.name: open console
data_flows.description: A duty engineer opens the dispatch console in a browser.
data_flows.source_excerpt: They open the dispatch console in their browser.
data_flows.notes: The engineer's sign-in method is not recorded.

data_flows.name: call API
data_flows.description: The dispatch console calls the dispatch API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console calls the dispatch API.
data_flows.notes: The console and API are served from different origins and the API answers cross-origin. Allowed origins and credential handling are not recorded.

data_flows.name: live job status
data_flows.description: The dispatch console opens and holds a WebSocket to the dispatch API for live job status.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console also opens a WebSocket to the dispatch API and holds it open for live job status.
data_flows.notes: Whether the socket runs over TLS, whether its handshake is authenticated, and whether it rechecks the engineer's session are not recorded.

data_flows.name: read and write database
data_flows.description: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.data_description: job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and creating tokens or sessions

data_flows.name: pull planned work
data_flows.description: The schedule importer pulls the partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every hour it pulls the partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS and parses the XML document it gets back.
data_flows.notes: How the partner identifies the importer and how the importer identifies the partner are not recorded.

data_flows.name: write archive
data_flows.description: The schedule importer writes each downloaded document into the schedule archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive

data_flows.name: post work orders
data_flows.description: The schedule importer posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API using an API token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The importer then posts the parsed work orders to the same dispatch API the console calls.
data_flows.notes: The API token was issued when the importer was built and has not been rotated since.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network where duty engineers and the schedule importer are located.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: production control plane
trust_boundaries.description: A same-company, higher-authority zone holding the live estate and capable of moving crews and changing depot work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The dispatch API runs in the production control plane.
trust_boundaries.notes: A corporate laptop holds none of the control-plane rights, and the control plane is not reachable from the internet.

trust_boundaries.name: scheduling partner
trust_boundaries.description: The zone controlled by the separate company that publishes planned work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company

assumptions.assumption: The corporate network is a network trust boundary because it is a distinct network location within the same company and authority.
assumptions.basis: The source explicitly places duty engineers and the schedule importer on the corporate network.

assumptions.assumption: The production control plane is a privilege trust boundary because it is controlled by the same company and staff but holds authority that corporate laptops do not.
assumptions.basis: The source says the control plane holds the live estate and can move a crew or change depot work, while a corporate laptop holds none of those rights.

assumptions.assumption: The scheduling partner is a tenant trust boundary because it is controlled by another company.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the scheduling partner is another company.

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch database is confidential because it contains personal data and credentials alongside operational job records.
assumptions.basis: The source states that it holds crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order.
